court: Court of Appeals for the First Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction over first petition after reconsideration granted
issues.why: Granting the reconsideration motion may have vacated the March 7 order, potentially mooting or affecting jurisdiction over petition No. 25-1340.

issues.label: Effect of consolidation of two petitions
issues.why: The court must determine how the consolidated petitions relate and which BIA order is properly under review.

issues.label: Ripeness of first petition filed pre-reconsideration ruling
issues.why: The April 7 petition was filed before the BIA ruled on the pending reconsideration motion, raising finality concerns.

issues.label: Standard of review for BIA determinations
issues.why: The court must apply substantial evidence to factual findings and de novo review to legal questions.

issues.label: Past persecution 'on account of family'
issues.why: Whether family constitutes a cognizable particular social group affects the nexus and the presumption of future persecution.

issues.label: Rebuttal via changed country conditions
issues.why: Whether police efforts against the Mungiki constitute a fundamental change sufficient to rebut the presumption must be assessed on substantial evidence.

issues.label: Rebuttal via applicant's changed age/status
issues.why: Whether Muchiri's adulthood and freedom from paternal control adequately rebut a well-founded fear of future persecution.

issues.label: DHS's burden to rebut presumption by preponderance
issues.why: The government bears the burden once past persecution is established, and the court must confirm that standard was met.

issues.label: Individualized analysis of changed conditions
issues.why: Changed country conditions must be tied to the applicant's specific circumstances, not generalized improvements.

issues.label: Consideration of all sources of past harm
issues.why: The BIA initially overlooked harm from age mates and other Mungiki members, raising whether the corrected record alters the analysis.

issues.label: Independent likelihood of future persecution
issues.why: Even absent past persecution presumption, the court must assess whether an independent well-founded fear exists.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum—severity of past persecution
issues.why: Whether the cumulative past harm was severe enough to warrant humanitarian asylum under 8 C.F.R. § 1208.13(b)(1)(iii)(A).

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum—other serious harm
issues.why: Whether a reasonable possibility of other serious harm on removal supports relief under the alternative prong.

issues.label: Discretionary denial for law-enforcement encounters
issues.why: The IJ's alternative discretionary denial based on U.S. law-enforcement encounters must be reviewed for adequacy and reviewability.

issues.label: Withholding of removal—clear probability standard
issues.why: Whether denial properly followed from asylum ineligibility and the 'unwilling or unable' government finding.

issues.label: Government 'unwilling or unable' to protect
issues.why: The IJ's finding on state protection is central to persecution by non-state actors like the Mungiki.

issues.label: CAT—more likely than not to be tortured
issues.why: Whether Muchiri showed likelihood of torture by or with acquiescence of public officials.

issues.label: CAT—government acquiescence given anti-Mungiki efforts
issues.why: Police efforts against the Mungiki may undercut any showing of official acquiescence to torture.

issues.label: Adequacy of BIA's reasoning on reconsideration
issues.why: Whether the BIA adequately explained why overlooked sources of harm did not change the outcome.

issues.label: Nature of Mungiki as persecutory group
issues.why: The record's inconsistent characterization (cult, gang, religion, tribe) affects the protected-ground and nexus analysis.

issues.label: Exhaustion of issues before the agency
issues.why: The court can review only issues Muchiri properly raised and exhausted before the BIA.

issues.label: Remand versus reversal as appropriate remedy
issues.why: The court must decide whether to reverse outright or remand for further factfinding under Ventura/Chenery principles.

issues.label: Effect of harm suffered as a child
issues.why: Whether persecution during childhood retains legal significance for present asylum and humanitarian claims.
